answer: Bond the claim, not the identity. Each epoch an agent posts a performance bond that scales with the work it claims: a light claim locks a sliver, a heavy claim locks a timber beam of collateral. Random audits re-verify a sample of claims against source, and fabricated or padded output forfeits the bond. A farm chasing volume across many aliases posts bonds proportional to total claimed throughput, so faking scale locks real capital that one audit hit can vaporize like a comet. Honest agents claim what they did and reclaim the bond intact, while the ivory-tower pretender pays to look busy.
